# Supreme AdBlock

> Supreme AdBlock is a free ad blocker extension for Chrome (and Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers) by Carbon Stealth. It stops YouTube video ads at the source, blocks banners, pop-unders, trackers and cookie walls, ships EasyList and EasyPrivacy built in, and updates its filter data twice a day with Ed25519-signed, data-only updates. No account, no analytics, no telemetry.

## Key facts

- Name: Supreme AdBlock
- Maker: Carbon Stealth VCC, Bulgaria (EU) — carbonstealth.eu, info@carbonstealth.eu
- Platform: Chrome Manifest V3 extension; Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers, version 121+
- Price: free, no account, no paid tier; optional donations
- Current version: 5.0.4 (24 September 2026)
- Homepage: https://adblock.carbonstealth.eu
- Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/chbjbiabkgocfbbfhednpbhfeipjcclk
- Privacy policy: https://adblock.carbonstealth.eu/privacy
- Licence: MIT; the shipped code is not minified or obfuscated

## What it does

- YouTube: the player request itself is flagged ad-free (isInlinePlaybackNoAd) and remaining ad fields are removed from responses; feed and search ads are removed too. It never blocks YouTube's video servers. If YouTube refuses playback on a flagged account, the extension steps aside for that session so videos still play.
- Filter lists: EasyList and EasyPrivacy compiled in (40,000+ network and cosmetic rules) plus an in-house set; tracking-parameter stripping (utm_*, fbclid, gclid); optional URLhaus malware-domain protection; third-party tracking cookies and beacons blocked.
- Signed updates: filter data (domains, CSS selectors, scriptlet directives) refreshes about twice a day, Ed25519-signed and version-locked. Only data is downloaded, never code.
- Anti-adblock: a scriptlet engine with 18 named routines (set-constant, abort-on-property-read, no-setTimeout-if, json-prune, no-fetch-if, …) runs before page scripts.
- Pop-unders: 2,700+ known pop-up ad hosts are refused at window.open.
- Cookie banners: presses the banner's own Reject button when there is one (Accept only as a last resort), then clears leftover blur, backdrops and scroll locks. It only presses a cookie banner's own buttons — never a sign-in, OAuth or payment button, never one that submits a form.
- Smart Detection: a list-free heuristic that hides cross-origin frames sized like ad slots.
- Controls: per-site allowlist, per-site switch for element hiding, element picker, procedural selectors, filter-list subscriptions by URL, a per-page breakdown of what each list blocked, an engine health card.
- Interface: English, Bulgarian, Italian, German.

## Privacy

Browsing data never leaves the device. The only automatic network request is the filter update (about twice a day); like any download it reaches the EU server with the user's IP address, and those requests are not logged. Optional sync uses the user's own browser account.

## Compared with uBlock Origin Lite

Both are free, Manifest V3, with EasyList and EasyPrivacy and no telemetry. uBlock Origin Lite's rules update with each extension release; Supreme AdBlock also updates signed filter data twice a day and adds list-free Smart Detection, a dedicated YouTube pipeline and cookie-banner handling.

## Common questions

Q: Is Supreme AdBlock free? A: Yes, with no account and no paid tier.
Q: Does it block YouTube ads? A: Yes, at the source, including feed and search ads.
Q: Does it collect data? A: No browsing data leaves the device; no analytics or telemetry.
Q: Will it break websites? A: Rarely; one click in the popup allows a site or turns off element hiding for it.
Q: Who makes it? A: Carbon Stealth VCC, a software studio in Bulgaria (EU).

_Last updated: 24 September 2026 (version 5.0.4)._
